features.title: Near-miss edge cases: a long spike row counts only once it is fully behind the spark, and standing or landing on a raised block is never a wall near miss
features.acceptance: A row of hazards (the contiguous run of hazard columns on the surface the spark runs on) fires its single near miss only once the spark's back edge has cleared the LAST column of the run, never while the spark is still over the row; a spark that lands on top of a raised block close to its edge, or stands on it, counts no wall near miss (a block below the spark is not a wall); a last-moment flip away from a raised wall still counts once; existing behaviour holds: an early flip and a death are not near misses, the count resets with each attempt, a checkpoint resume resets the tracker and flare but not the count; render-only (lib/sim, assets, android, ios, web, .github, pubspec.* unchanged); every existing test unchanged; analyzer clean and the full suite green.

Change: Gaze carries endCol (the contiguous run of hazard columns on that surface) and the tracker fires once the back edge passes endCol + 1; sparkGaze takes the spark's y, so a block the spark stands on or drops onto is not a wall; the tracker drops an armed wall when the spark stands on that surface overlapping the wall's columns (it can only be on top: a side hit is a death). Existing behaviour pinned: early flip 0, death 0, per-attempt reset, and a new test that a checkpoint resume keeps the count (passes on the old code too). flutter analyze: No issues found! flutter test: 226 passed / 3 skipped (baseline 219/3). git diff --stat origin/main -- lib/sim assets android ios web .github pubspec.yaml pubspec.lock = empty. Wall clause: the tracker still counts a wall escape once (unit test 'a wall the spark ends up standing on is disarmed; escaping to the other surface still fires': armed on a floor wall, over the row on the ceiling = no fire, past endCol on the ceiling = fires). In a real game that escape is not reachable today: a flip from the floor in front of a 1-tall block survives at alarm 0.5/0.55/0.6 and dies at 0.62/0.65/0.7 (one-off sweep on this branch; 0.7 also died on main), so with the 0.65 threshold no fresh-flip wall near miss can happen; the threshold is unchanged.
